title: Ifra Hormiz, Mother of King Shapur, King of Persia
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: She is mentioned favorably in Taanit 24b: she loved the sages of Israel in general and Rava in particular. Once Rava had a man flogged who had relations with a gentile woman, and he died. When it became known to King Shapur, he wanted to punish Rava, but his mother told him not to do any harm to the Jews, for whatever they ask of their Master He gives them; when they pray for rain, rain comes. He said to her: “If so, let them ask now, in the season of Tammuz, that rain fall.” She sent to Rava to pray for rain to fall, and so it was. In Bava Batra 8a she sent Rav Yosef a purse of dinars for a great mitzvah; there, 10b, she sent four hundred dinars to Rabbi Ami, who did not accept them, and she sent them to Rava, who accepted for the sake of peace with the government. In Zevachim 116b she sent Rava an offering to sacrifice for her for the sake of Heaven. In Niddah 20b she sent Rava blood, and he in his great wisdom understood that it was blood of desire. She said to her son: “See, my son, how wise the Jews are.” He said to her: “Perhaps like a blind man at a window.” She again sent him sixty kinds of blood, and Rava identified for all of them which kind of blood it was, except one kind of blood that he did not know. It happened that he sent her a comb that kills lice (she thought that this was why he sent her the comb). Then she said: “Jews, you dwell in the chambers of the heart.”

As for why she is called Ifra Hormiz, Rashi explains: she had the beauty of demons; Rabbeinu Tam explains: grace from the Omnipresent. The Gaon Shi”r, in Erekh Milin, p. 182, in Hyman’s judgment rightly proposed that Ifra is Persian for “the wife of” King Hormiz. Hyman reports that her son King Shapur was crowned while still in his mother’s womb, and his mother ruled in his name until he grew up, as cited in the chronicles of the kings of Persia.

notes.text: Saved Rashi Taanit24b’s שדים is clarified by saved Rashi Niddah20b linking Hormiz to Hormiz son of Lilith: beauty of demons, not breasts. The Tosafot24b request returned404, which proves no absence. כלמי means lice and the comb parenthesis is Hyman’s; Rashi, RabbeinuTam and Shi”r explanations and the womb-coronation chronology remain attributed alternatives, without new Persian etymology proof.

Directly consulted Rashi Niddah 20b explains Iphra and Hormiz through beauty and Hormiz son of Lilith, supporting demons rather than breasts. This does not independently establish Shi”r’s Persian etymology, Rabbeinu Tam’s exact reading or the womb-coronation chronology. The failed Tosafot request proves no absence. Lice, the comb parenthesis and the sixty-blood narrative remain as supplied.
